record.context_brief: best constant for the p >= 1 integral lower bound
record.original_question: Let p be a real number with p >= 1, let [a,b] be a real interval, and let f be a continuous function on [a,b]. Determine the best possible real constant alpha such that the lower integral inequality (e^p/(p^p alpha)) integral_a^b |f(x)|^p dx <= exp(integral_a^b |f(x)| dx) holds in the setting stated by the source.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. For p ≥1 a real number, determine the best possible constant α ∈R such that ep/(ppα)∫|f(x)|p dx ≤ exp(∫|f(x)| dx).
let f be a continuous function on [a, b]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p \geq 1$ be a real number, let $[a,b] \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a closed interval, and let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function. Determine the best possible (i.e., smallest) real constant $\alpha = \alpha(p,a,b) > 0$ such that the inequality
$$\frac{e^{p}}{p^{p}\,\alpha}\int_{a}^{b} |f(x)|^{p}\, dx \;\leq\; \exp\!\left(\int_{a}^{b} |f(x)|\, dx\right)$$
holds for every continuous function $f$ on $[a,b]$. In particular, identify $\alpha$ explicitly as a function of $p$ and the length $b-a$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches indicate this problem belongs to a family of open problems on integral inequalities posed by F. Qi that have attracted considerable attention, with several partial results and generalizations published. However, no source located explicitly identifies the best possible constant $\alpha$ in this specific exponential-type inequality, so the current status is not conclusively determined from the available search evidence.
